mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past 3 months compresses the risk-free rate, reducing the discount rate applied to future equity cash flows and generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods where FEDFUNDS has declined for 3 consecutive months, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate rises above 4.5% in a single month, it signals weakening labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of months where UNRATE exceeds 4.5%, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and consumer spending (RSAFS) indicates a broad-based weakening in the demand for goods and services, which triggers a sell-off in equities as corporate revenue expectations are revised downward, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods where both HOUST and RSAFS decline for 3 consecutive months, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of declining industrial production (INDPRO) below 110, supply chain disruptions and reduced manufacturing output lead to higher input costs and lower corporate margins, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods where INDPRO < 110, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real consumer spending (RSAFS) over the past 6 months signals strong household demand, which supports corporate revenue growth and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods where RSAFS has increased for 6 consecutive months, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the year-over-year change in CPI (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 3.0%, it signals accelerating inflation that prompts the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods where CPIAUCSL YoY > 3.0%, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in employment (PAYEMS) and an increase in unemployment (UNRATE) indicates a rapidly deteriorating labor market, which reduces consumer confidence and spending, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods where PAYEMS declines and UNRATE rises for 3 consecutive months, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 2.5% YoY) and rising interest rates (FEDFUNDS > 5.0%), the Federal Reserve's aggressive tightening cycle leads to reduced corporate investment and lower equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods where CPIAUCSL YoY > 2.5% and FEDFUNDS > 5.0%, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.
